## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Migaluddakapetavatthu* ("The Deer-Hunter (1st)", Pv 32) is a verse narrative in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text teaches that observing the moral precepts even for a brief duration yields beneficial karmic results [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral catalogs five translations of the poem across five languages [SuttaCentral].
Automated analysis by DharmaNexus indicates significant Pali-internal text reuse between this text and its companion story, the *Dutiyamigaluddakapetavatthu* (Pv 33), where a large segment (§3.4–11.1) closely mirrors Pv 33 (§4.4–12.1), as well as widespread overlap with its commentary in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language comparisons, DharmaNexus aligns sections of the text (notably §3.4) with Sanskrit parallels in the *Carmavastu* and the *Divyāvadāna*, alongside weaker alignments with the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
